THE TRIP

About the Spiti Valley Full Circuit

Spiti is India's first Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve. This circuit goes in through Shimla and Kinnaur and comes out through Chandratal and Manali, so the landscape keeps changing: green valleys and apple orchards first, then barren cliffs, ancient monasteries and high-altitude villages.

The route climbs gradually, which helps your body adjust to the altitude, and it covers the Kinnaur, Baspa and Spiti valleys in one trip. You travel with a tour leader and a group, with introductions, games and a certificate at the end.

WHAT AWAITS YOU

Major Trip Highlights

Kalpa — apple orchards, wooden houses and Kinnaur Kailash at sunset.

Chitkul — the last Indian village near the Indo-Tibet border.

Nako — the lake and village, and ancient monasteries.

Tabo Monastery — a monastery over 1,000 years old.

Key Monastery — the iconic monastery of Spiti.

Hikkim and Komic — the world's highest post office and one of the highest motorable villages.

Kunzum Pass — a crossing at 4,551 m.

Chandratal — the Moon Lake, with stargazing under clear skies.

DAY BY DAY

Your Itinerary

  • Pickup: 9:00 PM to 10:00 PM from Mayur Vihar Metro Station, Delhi. Departure at 10:00 PM.
  • Overnight journey: About 360 km and 8 to 9 hours by road via Ambala, Chandigarh and Solan to Shimla.
  • Meals: Dinner around midnight and breakfast in the morning, not included in the package.
  • Meet the group: Meet your fellow travellers and begin the journey towards the mountains.
  • Route: Shimla, Kufri, Narkanda, Rampur Bushahr, Jeori, Karcham and Reckong Peo to Kalpa. About 230 km, 8 to 9 hours.
  • Road: A scenic drive along the Sutlej River. Smooth till Rampur, rough patches near Karcham.
  • Reckong Peo: Stop at the viewpoint for a first glimpse of Kinner Kailash.
  • Kalpa: Explore the village of apple orchards and wooden houses, and watch the sunset over Kinnaur Kailash.
  • Stay: Homestay in Kalpa, with dinner.
  • Note: A long travel day: hydrate well and avoid alcohol. Acclimatisation starts here, and nights are cold.
  • Route: Kalpa, Reckong Peo, Karcham, Sangla and Chitkul. About 90 km, 4 to 5 hours.
  • Chitkul: Visit the last Indian village near the Indo-Tibet border, along the Baspa River.
  • Baspa Valley: Riverside walks, with snow peaks against the green valley.
  • Sangla: Sunset views in Sangla.
  • Stay: Hotel or homestay in Sangla, with breakfast and dinner.
  • Note: Roads are narrow so driving is slow. Carry snacks as options are limited in Chitkul.
  • Route: Sangla, Reckong Peo, Karcham, Powari, Pooh, Khab (Sutlej and Spiti confluence) and Nako. About 130 km, 4 to 5 hours.
  • Landscape: Green valleys give way to cold desert mountains through remote Upper Kinnaur villages.
  • Nako: Visit Nako Lake at sunset, and explore the village and its ancient monasteries.
  • Stay: Hotel or homestay in Nako, with breakfast and dinner.
  • Note: A big altitude gain today, so walk slowly and stay hydrated. It can turn cold and windy in Nako.
  • Route: Nako, Malling Nallah, Tabo, Dhankar and Kaza. About 115 km, 6 to 7 hours.
  • Malling Nallah: One of the more challenging road sections in Spiti, so we start early.
  • Tabo: Visit the Tabo Monastery, over 1,000 years old, and walk through the village.
  • Dhankar: Optional visit to Dhankar Monastery and its viewpoint.
  • Kaza: Arrive in Kaza, the heart of Spiti Valley.
  • Stay: Homestay in Kaza, with breakfast and dinner.
  • Route: Kaza, Key Monastery, Chicham Bridge, Langza, Hikkim, Komic and back to Kaza. About 80 to 100 km round trip.
  • Key Monastery: Visit the iconic Key Monastery.
  • Hikkim: The world's highest post office.
  • Komic: One of the world's highest motorable villages.
  • Langza: Fossil hunting and the large Buddha statue.
  • Stay: Hotel in Kaza, with breakfast and dinner.
  • Note: High altitude, so walk slowly. Carry sunscreen, sunglasses, water and energy snacks.
  • Route: Kaza, Losar, Kunzum Pass, Batal and Chandratal. About 90 km, 6 to 7 hours.
  • Kunzum Pass: Cross the pass at 4,551 m.
  • Road: One of the toughest stretches, with rocky off-road terrain after Kunzum Pass.
  • Chandratal: Visit Chandratal (Moon Lake) and stargaze under clear skies.
  • Stay: Camps near Chandratal, with breakfast and dinner.
  • Note: There is no lakeside camping because of eco rules. It is extremely cold at night and facilities are basic.
  • Route: Chandratal, Batal, Gramphu, Atal Tunnel and Manali. About 130 km, 7 to 9 hours.
  • Road: Rough terrain till Gramphu, then smooth roads after the Atal Tunnel.
  • Manali: A comfortable descent after the high altitude, with time in Manali before the overnight journey.
  • Meals: Breakfast included.
  • Note: Start early because of road conditions, and expect delays near water crossings.
  • Departure: 8:00 PM to 9:00 PM from Manali.
  • Overnight journey: About 450 km and 10 to 11 hours via Mandi, Chandigarh and Ambala.
  • Arrival: Early morning in Delhi at Mayur Vihar Metro Station, where the trip ends.
  • Meals: Breakfast in the morning, not included.
  • Certificate: A certificate for completing the Spiti Circuit Expedition.
WHAT YOU PAY FOR

Inclusions & Exclusions

Included in your package

  • 1 night in a homestay in Kalpa
  • 1 night in a homestay in Sangla
  • 1 night in a homestay in Nako
  • 2 nights in a hotel or homestay in Kaza
  • 1 night in camps near Chandratal
  • Meals: 6 breakfasts and 6 dinners
  • An experienced tour leader
  • All transport from Delhi to Kaza and back, as per the itinerary
  • All necessary permits, including inner line permits
  • Fuel, driver charges, tolls and parking
  • Fun group games and introductions, and a certificate on completion

Not included in your package

  • Lunches, snacks and beverages during transit or at cafes
  • Dinner and breakfast on the two overnight journeys
  • Personal expenses such as laundry, shopping and phone calls
  • Entry tickets, camera fees or activity charges at monuments and sightseeing points
  • Non-vegetarian meals
  • Tours or excursions not mentioned in the itinerary
  • Medical or travel insurance
  • Extra costs due to landslides, roadblocks, strikes or natural calamities
  • Tips for drivers, guides or hotel staff
  • Anything not listed under inclusions
